I checked these claims and they hold:
- **Link key inputs.** The link key holds argv, rsp, the sha256 of each input, LIB/LIBPATH, the toolchain and build_env_id() (buildcache.py:735-739). build_env_id() is host, wine and prefix (buildcache.py:164-173).
- **Miss counts.** I counted again over 55 runs: 5 runs miss 0 links, 30 miss 1, 8 miss 2, 2 miss 3 and 10 miss 5. This agrees with the answer. One more run came in while the solver worked.
- **scd-01a/97129 cause.** Base c4cd145 is the parent commit. `git diff --stat` shows that src/Server/BloodLib/source/DaemonConfig.cpp changed. DaemonConfig.cpp.obj is in the rsp of all 5 exes. So cause (a) is confirmed.
- **gc.** gate.log says removed 0.
- **Results.** gate.log:60-69 gives new MATCH 0 for all 5 exes.

I did not check these numbers again: the CPU-s figures (median 0, p90 256, sum 1887), the wall-tail figures (sum 316) and the contention figures (11-15 s vs 41-52 s).

On the proposal:
- The early-fail idea is sound and cheap, but its gain is small. It saves about 1-4 min per wave, and the solver marks this with ❓. It saves 0 tokens. The solver says these limits honestly.
- Risk 1: the early-fail rule skips the off-target regression signal in failed rounds. The author's next round can then hide a shared-code MATCH -> DIFF until a later round. That round still gets the full check before credit, so credit stays safe.
- Risk 2: the rule needs a parity.sh change in bns-lift. That change is the C++ lift tooling, not the engine.

The analysis correctly rejects Options 1 and 2 with evidence.

In the v2b wave, 4 of the 8 author.py runs ended "parked". Together they cost about 2.12M of the 3.31M author cost units (64 %). The data comes from the first line of /data/parity-v2/v2batch/results/v2b-*.author.log:

- lg-01a: 486,771 units, and scd-01a: 395,679 units. Park proof_blocked: "main 55e17ad176 moved after the proof base c4cd145654; run check again". The rule is cardrun.py:1186-1187, and author.py:1307 maps it to a park.
- pod-01: 821,978 units. Park proof_blocked: "integrate refuses: review items without a valid accept receipt ... PostOfficeDaemon wmain: reject".
After these parks, the operator wrote the new cards lg-01b, lg-01c and scd-01b. These cost a further 993k units.
Answer these questions:
(1) For each parked run, did the committed tree at park time already hold MATCH gains? Use the proof logs under /data/parity-v2/author/<card>/ and the *.recheck.log files. Did a later recheck or land with no new author session recover those gains, or did a new author session buy the same items again? Compare the item lists in v2batch/cards/v2b-lg-01*.md and v2b-scd-01*.md.
(2) How many units would 3 fixes save, and how many MATCH would they lose? Fix A: on "main moved", rebase the committed tree and run the proof again, with no park. Fix B: at a context split with no file change, hand off once before you park. Fix C: drop only the rejected review item, and do not park the whole card.
(3) Give the new tokens per MATCH for the wave with these fixes, and compare it with 84k nocr per MATCH. Use the ledger credit rows (pod-01 4, wmain-01 3, cg-02 1).
(4) Give the wall time of each parked run and of each re-authored card. Use the author state.json timestamps. Say how much of the 1-hour goal the fixes win.
why: The lessons so far cover cache writes per message and duplicate reviews. No lesson covers whole author sessions that end in a park for a reason outside the code: a concurrent land moved main, a split hit a hard cap, or one review was rejected. These parks are the largest single token sink: 64 % of author units, with no credit. Two of the 4 parks come from a race with the land of a sibling card. A rebase-and-reprove path costs one build, which is about 600-900 s per the walltime lesson, and no author tokens. If the parked trees held real gains, the fix cuts author units per MATCH by up to about 2x. That alone can move v2 from 136-160k per MATCH to below 84k.
answer: The premise does not hold. Of the 4 parked trees, only pod-01 held MATCH gains (4: Console::Flush and wmain$dtor$0 absent->MATCH, operator delete[] and wmain DIFF->MATCH). An operator commit (f8f975a, 5 lines) recovered them with no new author session, and the card landed with credit 4. The lg-01a and scd-01a trees had 0 gain, and their rechecks (which already rebase) came back ready with match_gain 0. lg-01 committed nothing. The re-authored cards lg-01b, lg-01c and scd-01b took the remaining items of the split-up cards, not the same items again, and all gave 0 MATCH. question:
The vsobj object cache is per host, and a new remote slot starts cold. Does that cold start cost more than the remote run saves, and which warm-up and placement rule gives the shortest wave?

Facts from the 2026-11-26 v2b-lg/scd author gates:

| Run | Host | vsobj restore (entries/restored) | vsobj record (new/known) | push s | run s | pull s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| lg-01b | build3 slot 1 | – | 354/0 | 42.7 | 149.1 | 1.5 |
| lg-01c | build3 | 0/0 | 5/349 | 3.3 | 135.8 | 1.3 |
| lg-01a | local | 364/280 | 74/280 | – | 196 | – |
| scd-01a | local | 622/263 | 91/263 | – | 229 | – |

- All runs use the same namespace 42fe8338…
- build3 had obj=false in remote.json. The build3 funcdiff cache was warm: "cached=2204 new=0".
- On build3, parity_sh took 120 s of the 149 s run (gate.phases).
- lg-01c restored 0 entries. When it recorded, build3 knew 349. So lg-01b filled the host store while lg-01c was already running.

Questions:
(a) Look at every gate.log, gate.phases and remote.json under gap/ and in the remote.jsonl log for this wave. Split the job seconds into push, gate_sh, parity_sh and pull. Group the jobs by host and by vsobj restored/entries (cold = 0, warm > 0). How many seconds does a cold vsobj start add per job on build2, on build3 and on the local host? How many seconds does the first-push (42.7 s) penalty add?
(b) Where do the vsobj store and the remote fd/funcdiff store live (remote_build.py:719, 812-851; buildcache.py)? Does any code path copy a new vsobj namespace from a remote host back to the local host, or from one host to another? If one host dies, how many cold-start seconds does the next host pay to take its jobs?
(c) Compare two plans for a wave of N author gates over 3 hosts (8 local cores, build2 4 slots, build3 6 slots):
  1. Before the wave, run one "seed" gate per host per namespace, or rsync the vsobj namespace to each host.
  2. Send the first job of each namespace to the local host only, then fan out.
Give the minutes each plan saves against the 60-minute goal. Give the extra tokens per MATCH that each plan costs (expected: 0, because no model call is made).
why: Remote gate runs are already shorter than local runs: 136-149 s on build3, against 196-229 s local and the 617-921 s local tail of lesson [walltime L3]. But each host or slot that starts a namespace pays a cold vsobj start ("known 0") and a first push of up to 42.7 s. When jobs spread over 3-4 hosts and a dead host moves its jobs to another host, these cold starts can multiply. Earlier questions covered objsync on/off, slot counts and transport cool-down. No question has yet measured the vsobj warm-up cost per host and namespace, or a seed/placement rule. A pre-wave seed or a namespace-aware dispatch is a small slotq/remote_build change. It costs no model tokens, so all of its gain goes to the 1-hour goal.
answer:
No. A cold vsobj start does not cost more than the remote run saves. A fully cold build3 job (run 136-149 s; 141-195 s with push and pull) beats a warm local job (177-229 s). The local host is slow because of load: link 34-54 s per exe against 5-9 s on build3, fd 56-69 s against 12 s, and gate_sh 83-125 s against 22-27 s.

(a) Phase split.
- build3 cold: lg-01b push 42.7, gate_sh 27.4, parity_sh 120.2, pull 1.5. lg-01c push 3.3, gate_sh 21.9, parity_sh 112.4, pull 1.3.
- local partial warm (74-91 misses): parity_sh 106-108 s. Local all-hit (scd-01b): parity_sh 10.5 s, but restore 36.7 s.
- Cold start adds about 85-93 s per job on build3 (warm card 27.0 s from OBJ-CACHE §3.3) ❓, about 124 s on build2 (166.3 against 41.9, cl_jobs 2), and 95 s or more on local ❓.
- The first push adds 39.4 s, once per slot.
- Every job that starts on a host before the first record of the namespace is cold. The window is about 136-149 s, so build3 can pay this up to 6 times per namespace.

(b) Stores.
- Local: /data/parity-v2/build-cache/gate, with vsobj/<ns>/index.jsonl.
- Remote: one R/store per host (remote_build.py:425), shared by all slots. Preview caches are per slot.
- The namespace is the same on all hosts because BUILD_HOSTNAME is the main host name.
- The only copy path is objsync.py through objsync_hook (remote_build.py:318-350). It is off and not set in hosts.json, so nothing was copied in this wave. No path copies directly from host to host. Nothing copies cc, link or fd entries.
- Dead host: the failed job waits for a local slot (slotq.py:45), which costs 140-170 s more than a warm remote. The next remote host pays 85-124 s per cold job, and 39 s per slot it has never used.
- free_hosts sorts by most free slots first, which spreads cold starts.

(c) Plans.
- Plan 1 (seed with objsync push at about 5 s per host, plus a pre-pushed base clone) saves about 2 min on a normal wave and 4-6 min with a dead host.
- Plan 2 (first job on local) loses 0.5-1.5 min. Remote hosts stay cold anyway, because objsync is off.
- Both plans cost 0 tokens per MATCH.

subject: safety
question:
The review carry treats one model verdict as a fixed fact. It reuses an earlier verdict when all 7 key parts match (exe, symbol, cand fp, orig digest, checker digest, review digest, bundle digest). Ledger code: parityctl/ledger.py:431-521. Card ledger code: receipts.local_carry_source at receipts.py:376-388. The ledger shows that the reviewer is not deterministic on identical input. In /data/parity-v2/ledger/events.jsonl there are 360 origin review events (278 accept, 79 reject, 3 park) and 177 groups of (exe, symbol, cand fp, review digest). In 8 of these groups the verdicts disagree. In some groups the bundle digest is also the same:
- LobbyJob::transit, fp 863495b8, bundle 44d47d1b: accept, accept, reject.
- LobbyJobManager::find, fp 8f39cf3b, bundle 046368df: reject ×7 and accept ×1 across review digests 76e363, 40132f and 4d922a.
Also, for wmain (fp 6a33ba64, card v2b-pod-01), bundle 6ef4db15 got reject and bundle 8b27be3b got accept. The bundle includes the lift source text (review.py:826, lift_source), so a source edit that leaves the code the same can give a new bundle digest and a new draw.
Question:
(a) Give the true verdict flip rate on exact-same 7-part keys. Then give the probability that one draw gives a false accept, using the items that got a reject in at least one draw.
(b) find_carry returns None on a conflict (ledger.py:513). But the first accept carries until a second draw happens, and in the normal flow a second draw never happens. So does the carry lock in a lucky accept, and does integrate.py then give MATCH credit for it? Name the code path.
(c) Can an author re-roll a reject by a comment-only edit in the source? Count the cases in the ledger and in the card receipts dbs where the cand fp is the same, the review digest is the same, only the bundle digest changes, and the verdict goes from reject to accept.
(d) Propose a rule that keeps the carry cheap and safe. Examples: carry an accept only after 2 agreeing draws; make the bundle digest leave out comment-only source lines; or require a fresh second draw when an earlier receipt for the same fp was a reject. Give its extra token cost per wave and per MATCH. Use the real review tokens per call from the card receipts usage, and compare with the 84k-per-MATCH goal.
why: Speed and cost plans reuse review verdicts (carry, local carry, cache by bundle digest). Earlier lessons say that review costs are under 1 % of wave tokens and that the cache key must keep the bundle digest. They assume that a verdict is a stable function of its key. The ledger shows that this is false: identical keys give both accept and reject. So a cached accept can be a false MATCH that the skeptic gate would reject in 1 of 2 or more draws. Bundle re-rolls also let an author shop for an accept. The answer gives a measured false-accept risk and a carry rule (2-of-2 accept, or a comment-insensitive bundle digest) at a known token price. This keeps the review gate strong and still uses less than 1 % of the 1 h / 84k budget.
answer:
(a) On exact 7-part keys: 76 groups with >=2 accept/reject draws (252 draws). 3 groups disagree, so the group flip rate is 3.9 % and the pair flip rate is 5/322 = 1.6 %. With 4 key parts it is 6/75 (8 %). With 3 parts it is 7/38 (18 %). On items with >=1 reject, an accept draw is a false accept in 4/31 = 12.9 % of draws (pooled 7-part; mean per-item p = 15 %). On bundles with a known defect it is 5/20 = 25 %. The reasons show real defects: a wrong addReferenceCount overload (PDB name) in find, and the _state read moved across a virtual call in transit (❓). None of these accepts got credit.
(b) Yes, it locks in. The first draw is final: receipts.py:50 makes (proof, exe, symbol, review_digest) the primary key, and review.py:833 reuses the 'have' receipt. The carry spreads that draw: cardrun.py:981 carry -> receipts.local_carry_source:376, and cardrun.py:985 global_carry -> ledger.carry_into:606 -> find_carry:521 (one origin draw, no conflict) -> receipts.carry_review:343. Then integrate.check_review:106 accepts and credit():123 counts it as MATCH. Carried events never add draws (review_index :489), and a conflict (:513) only starts one fresh draw, which is also final. The carry has not run yet (0 carried events or rows). Over the history, 2 groups had a first-draw accept that a later draw rejected.
(c) A comment-only edit cannot re-roll: lift_source strips comments and blank lines (review.py:356, 425), and the line number is not in the bundle. The ledger has 4 reject->accept changes with the same fp and review digest and only a new bundle (find x3, wmain x1). The receipt dbs have 3 groups (wmain pod-01, wmain cg-02 with a different fp, ZSTD_litLengthPrice with fp ❓). All 4 ledger cases are real PDB mangled-name fixes that the strict cand fp does not see (A-section diff verified for wmain). I found 0 cosmetic re-rolls, but a format-only or rename edit could still do one ❓.
(d) Cost of the rule: R1 (an accept needs 2 agreeing draws) adds 3 x 3,883 = 11.6k tokens per v2b wave, which is 1.46k per MATCH (1.7 % of 84k). Wall time is 0 s with a parallel draw and <=10 s per accept if serial. R2 (a deterministic precheck for callee mangled names) costs 0 tokens and removes 2 of the 5 measured false-accept draws. No speed gain toward the 1 h goal.

proposal:
Change 3 things.
(1) review.py precheck (:259): add the rule P4_callee_name. It sets precheck to reject when a call or jump target in the A section has 'original only' and 'build only' mangled function names that differ in the parameter or type part. A difference only in the data access code (@@0 vs @@2) does not count. It costs 0 tokens and is deterministic. It closes the PDB-name hole that the strict fp does not see: 2 of the 5 measured false-accept draws (find 5f6a17d6 and 046368df), plus wmain 6ef4db15.
(2) The 2-draw accept rule. In review.py decide() (and review86), when the first draw on a bundle is an accept, start a second draw on the same bundle in parallel. Record an accept only when both draws are accepts; a split counts as a reject with reason 'split'. Store both reply digests. In ledger.carriable (:493) and receipts.carriable (:363), carry an accept only when the key has >=2 agreeing origin accepts and no reject. Leave out carried events as before. Cost: +1 call per accept, which is about 11.6k tokens per v2b wave and 1.46k tokens per MATCH (1.7 % of the 84k goal). Wall time: +0 s in parallel, <=10 s per accept if serial. The false-accept rate on defective items falls from about 15 % to about 8 % (mean p^2); with P4 it falls further.
(3) Keep the bundle digest in all keys, because real fixes change it (4/4 measured reject->accept cases). Also normalize S (collapse whitespace) before the digest, so a format-only edit cannot buy a new draw.
Tests:
- Replay the 76 multi-draw groups. The new carry must carry 0 accepts from a group that has a reject.
- Use the 3 defect bundles as golden fixtures. P4 must reject them, and the 66 all-accept groups must still pass P4.
- Canary: carry_into with 1 accept gives no carry; with 2 agreeing accepts it carries.
- A whitespace-only lift edit must give the same bundle digest.
Gain: 0 % of the 1 h speed goal. Cost is +1.7 % of the per-MATCH budget. A single lucky draw can no longer lock in a false MATCH.

- The rule that a split vote counts as a reject can lose real MATCHes.
- The proposal gives no speed gain toward the 1-hour goal.
- The cost is good: about +1.5k tokens per MATCH, which is about 1.7 % of the 84k budget.
- The P4 rule for callee mangled names costs 0 tokens and is a good, deterministic fix.

subject: measure
question:
The ledger can now give a per-step timeline for one card. But can it give the wall time of a whole wave, and the split of that time across steps, without double counting? The data in /data/parity-v2/ledger/events.jsonl (623 events, 204 kind=build) shows these facts:
(a) Build events have `at` and `seconds`, but no t0. ledger.append (ledger.py:249-250) sets `at` to the write time when the caller gives none. So t0 = at - seconds is only a guess (❓ is `at` always written at step end?).
(b) Steps nest. For v2b-pod-01 (times in s after the first v2b event at 13:47:24Z), `author.proof` runs from 821 to 2084 (1262.82 s). It contains `full_build` (822-1839, 1017 s), `base_build` (1847-2061, 213 s), `strict` and `proof`. If you add the per-step sums over the 15 v2b cards, you get about 16,700 s: full_build 7028, author.proof 4139, author.session 2034, author.build_gate 1373, base_build 1031. That sum counts the nested time twice.
(c) The first v2b event is at 13:47:24Z and the last is 5059 s later (about 84 min). But the owner says a wave takes 4-5 h, and wave-4exe-start.txt says 09:06:23Z. No event has a `wave` id, and no event marks the wave start, queue entry or the end of the last test.
Questions:
(1) For the 2026-11-26 v2b wave, what are the true wave start and end? Use wave-4exe-start.txt, the author state.json step starts, the cardrun dirs and the run.log TIMING lines. How many seconds of the 4-5 h fall outside the first and last ledger event, and which step owns them (card writing, queue wait, slot wait, review, landq)?
(2) Inside the ledger span, find the critical path. Use only the non-nested steps (session, commit, build_ref/noref, full_build, base_build, strict, proof, review, land). How many seconds does each step add to the critical path, and how many seconds are idle gaps between steps? Which step must shrink to reach 1 h?
(3) Give the smallest instrumentation change. For example: each build event gets `t0`, `parent_step` (so nested steps are not summed), `host`, `slot` and `wave`, and the scheduler writes `wave_start` and `wave_end` events. With that change, can one query give "wave wall time = sum of critical-path steps + idle gaps", so that each speed change is proven with numbers?
why: The 1 h goal needs a correct baseline. Today the ledger seems to show 84 min for v2b, but the owner reports 4-5 h. One of these numbers is wrong, or most of the time is outside the ledger. Also, a naive sum of step seconds (about 16,700 s) counts nested steps such as author.proof ⊃ full_build twice. If nobody fixes this, a speed change can look like a win or a loss when it is neither. If we know the critical path and the idle gaps in seconds, we know which step (full_build is about 1017 s on pod-01) or which wait to attack first, and how many minutes of the 1 h goal each fix wins.
answer: The two numbers measure different waves. The 4-5 h is most likely the manual 4exe wave: 09:06:23Z to 12:52:23Z = 13,560 s (3 h 46 min), with 0 ledger events. ❓ Another possible source: HANDOFF.md has false clock times written by the lead (13:35 to 19:20, 5 h 45 min). Example: "18:10 merge-01 LANDED", but git e25645b is 15:05:42Z. The v2b wave ran from 13:27:08Z (lead transcript) to 15:16:35Z (merge-02 land) = 6,567 s (1 h 49 min). Inside the ledger (5,408 s), adding all steps gives 16,840 s and adding leaf steps gives 12,701 s, so 4,139 s are counted twice. The real critical path is the land chain (pod-01, wmain-01, cg-02, merge-01, merge-02): full_build 2,554 s (47 %), wait before the landing card's first step 983 s, idle inside segments 620 s (1,603 s idle in total, 30 %), author.session 440 s, base_build 383 s, build_ref+noref 293 s, other steps 133 s. full_build is the step that must shrink. pod-01's first full_build took 1,017 s against a median of about 215 s. Failed and killed steps are dropped (:498): 7 steps, 15 s in this wave. Lead tokens: nocr 1.43M (meter.py), about 143k per MATCH for about +10 MATCH ❓. Two early background searches (a find and a recursive grep over the cardrun slot folders) were stopped at their 10-minute limit. question:
The author step already builds and compares the card. Does cardrun then repeat that work for no reason?

Background, with evidence:
- author.py:784-815 (compare_gate) runs a gate build of the card and compares the MATCH count of each exe with the base. The result goes to author/<card>/state.json 'compare'.
- For lg-01a, lg-01b, lg-01c, scd-01a and scd-01b, that compare shows gain 0 and card_gain 0. The author gate logs are build-gate-r01.log and build-gate-r02.log. One of them reports "build3 slot 2: gate_fast.sh rc 0 (135.8 s)".

Cardrun state.json then ran full_build again with reused=false: lg-01a 247 s and 339 s, lg-01b 253 s and 202 s, lg-01c 188 s, scd-01a 245 s, scd-01b 149 s. The base_build steps add 76 s and 76 s, and strict and proof run after that. The cardrun dry_check gives match_gain 0 for all five, and they end as 'ready' with nothing to credit.

Answer these:

(2) When the rev, the checkers digest and the toolchain are the same, can cardrun use the author gate build dir and its <Exe>.funcdiff.json for full_build? subject: walltime
question:
With a warm cache, the gate_sh phase (bns-lift tools/gate.sh in gate_fast.sh:61) is still the largest phase of a v2b full build. It takes 48-220 s, and parity_sh (funcdiff) takes 8-230 s. Most of gate_sh is not compiling. In 5 warm builds (cc hits 383-387 of 391), the time from the last cc event in build-vs2010/cache-events.jsonl to the gate_sh end is 37-178 s. Examples: cg-01 full-d789726212 has 1 s before cc, 39 s of cc and 178 s after cc (218 s total). lg-01b full-91913409c5 has 41 s of cc and 171 s after cc. merge-02 full-e76b748e82 has 7 s of cc and 40 s after cc. After the last compile, gate.sh does these steps: the remaining clang-cl/lld links and static libs (ninja shows 411 steps), tools/gate_extra.sh → tools/run_selftest.sh (a second `cmake --build --target lift_selftest`, then lift_selftest.exe under wine), and tools/pdb_layout.py build/ for lift_marketdealerdaemon. None of these steps goes through buildcache.

(1) For all 28 v2b full builds in /data/parity-v2/cardrun/slot*/lift-lobbydaemon-v2b-*/full-*, split the post-cc tail of gate_sh into link, selftest (build + wine run) and pdb_layout. Use the cache-events 't' values, the gate.phases values, file mtimes in clone/build/ (the .lib/.exe/.pdb outputs, lift_selftest.exe) and the gate.log lines. If that is not enough, time each step once on a warm clone outside the engine. Give the median and the max per step.
(2) Why does the same warm tail take 40 s in one build and 178 s in another? Compare the windows with the other gate.log windows that ran at the same time (cg-01 and lg-01b ran with 3-4 parallel slots on 8 local cores; cl_jobs/link_jobs are in build.json). Is it CPU contention, the wine start, or the disk?
(3) Propose one change that takes this tail off the card critical path. Examples: make the clang-cl links and pdb_layout content-keyed in buildcache (the key is the input .obj/.lib hashes), or skip them on a hit. Run gate_extra.sh at the same time as vsobj_restore + parity_sh, because parity_sh does not use build/. Or skip the clang link when the card does not touch lift_selftest/lift_marketdealerdaemon sources. Give the seconds saved per card build (median and max), the seconds saved per 6-card wave on the land chain, and the share of the 1-hour goal that the change wins. Confirm that the change keeps the same gate verdict (rc and "gate ok"/"selftest ok" lines) for at least 2 builds.
why: Earlier lessons fixed the gc tail, the clone/push and the cold ledger numbers. The next biggest warm-cache cost is inside gate_sh, and it is not compiling: 37-178 s per build runs after the last cc event, outside buildcache, and in series before parity_sh. With 28 full builds in v2b and about 2-4 full builds on the land chain per card, moving or caching this tail can save about 40-170 s per build. That is about 5-25 % of the 1-hour goal per wave (❓ the exact land-chain count needs checking). Of all the phases still open, it has the clearest path to a fix.
answer:
## Summary
I measured it. The warm tail of gate_sh is almost all `tools/pdb_layout.py`. The clang links take 0.0-0.4 s. The selftest build plus its wine run takes less than 1 s.

Each run of pdb_layout parses all 345 checked .cpp files again with clang-cl (`/Zs -fdump-record-layouts-complete`). That costs about 213 CPU-s, and no cache covers it. The wall time is fixed by how many free cores there are.

## Build count
There are 31 `full-*` dirs. 28 of them have a `gate.phases` file. Three have none: merge-03d, merge-02/08e86, merge-03c. All the numbers below use the 28.

## (1) How the tail splits

| Step | How I measured it | Median | Max |
|---|---|---|---|
| Links and libs (last cc `t` → newest `build/*.exe,*.lib` mtime) | 28 builds | 0.1 s | 0.4 s |
| Selftest: `cmake --build --target lift_selftest` (no-op) + run under wine | ninja dry-run 0.02 s; wine run 0.15 / 0.03 / 0.03 s, read-only sandbox on cg-01 | <1 s | <1 s |
| pdb_layout (newest output mtime → gate_sh end) | 28 builds | 80.0 s | 177.6 s (min 34.0 s, sum 2,312 s) |

Cost of pdb_layout, from 30 sample TUs run serially:
- The clang part takes 0.604 CPU-s per TU. For 345 TUs that is about 208-213 CPU-s.
- The Python parse takes 0.018 CPU-s per TU, about 6.4 s. It runs on one thread.
- `own_names` takes 0.08 s.
- The resym dumps are already cached in `home/.cache/bns-lift/resym`.

## (2) Why one tail is 40 s and another is 178 s
The cause is CPU contention. It is not the wine start and it is not the disk.

- pdb_layout uses `ThreadPoolExecutor(os.cpu_count())`, which gives 8 threads.
- With no other gate running, the tail is 34-42 s (5 builds). That equals 213 CPU-s on about 5.3-6.5 effective cores.
- cg-01/d789 (178 s) and lg-01b/9191 (171 s) each ran beside 2.0 other builds. Of that load, 1.6-1.7 builds were in their own pdb_layout and 0.3-0.4 in cc. Their effective cores were 1.24-1.29.
- The tail correlates with the overlap of other builds' pdb_layout + cc windows: Pearson r = 0.81 over the 28 builds. With all other phases, r = 0.69.
- The wine run takes 0.03-0.15 s, so wine is not the cause.
- The disk is not the cause either. The resym cache hits. The headers come from the same tree that cc read a few seconds earlier, so they are probably still in the page cache ❓.
- The cause is ❓ for two builds: wmain-01 (80 s) and merge-03 (103 s). They had no other v2b gate or strict step running at the same time. A load from outside v2b is likely ❓. As a reference, the load average was 12-25 today while cargo ran.

## (3) Gain from the proposal
The proposal is to key pdb_layout by content. Details are in the proposal field. The residual time is an estimate of about 4 s ❓.

- **Per card build:** saves 76 s median and 174 s max. Over the 28 builds that is 2,200 s.
- **CPU freed:** about 213 CPU-s per build, about 6,000 CPU-s per wave. This also shortens the cc and parity_sh phases of the other slots ❓.
- **Land chain:** 5 v2b cards landed with 9 full builds (ledger). Their tails sum to 574 s, a mean of 63.8 s, which is 1.8 builds per card.
- **Per 6-card wave on the land chain:** about 6 × 1.8 × 60 s ≈ 650 s if the land chain runs one card after another. It is about 215 s if 4 slots make it about 2 cards deep ❓.
- **Share of the 1-hour goal:** 6-18 % (215-650 s of 3,600 s).

The other option is to run gate_extra at the same time as vsobj_restore + parity_sh. It saves at most 45 s median and 103 s max per build (1,436 s in total). It still burns the 213 CPU-s, and those CPU-s then compete with funcdiff. So the cache option is better.

## Verdict check
- All 30 gate.logs with a verdict have `selftest ok`, `gate ok` and `pdb_layout … 0 errors`. There are only 2 different pdb_layout lines: 26× "1763 classes, 6522 members" and 4× "1790 classes, 6567 members". All 28 builds with phases have rc = 0.
- The cache depends on the dumps being deterministic, so I tested that. The layout dumps of CryptoKey.cpp, CacheD.cpp and LobbyDaemon.cpp are byte-identical (same sha256) in two clones at different revisions: cg-01 d789726 and merge-02 e76b748. Because the content is the same, the cached records give the same verdict. I could not run the changed gate, because I had read-only access.
evidence: bns-lift tools/gate_extra.sh:5-7: run_selftest.sh, then pdb_layout.py. tools/pdb_layout.py:128-136 runs clang_dump (/Zs -fdump-record-layouts-complete) for every .cpp. :190-191 runs ThreadPoolExecutor(os.cpu_count()) with no cache. :60 caches only the resym dump.
/tmp/split.py over 28 phased builds: link = last build/*.exe|*.lib mtime minus last cc t = 0.0-0.4 s. The tail after the links is median 80.0 s, max 177.6 s, min 34.0 s, sum 2,312 s.
cg-01/full-d789726212: gate_sh 1795705003.66-1795705221.64. Last cc at about 043.85. CacheGate.exe mtime 1795705044.01, lift_selftest.exe 041.23. So 177.6 s ran after the last output.
Sample (30 TUs, cg-01 clone, read-only bwrap): cpu_per_tu 0.604 s, wall 97.7 s at nice 10 under load 12-24. 345 TUs are checked (353 .cpp minus lift_selftest 8 and lift_zstd).
Python parse 0.018 CPU-s per TU, own_names 0.08 s. Selftest wine run 0.145/0.026/0.029 s with output 'lift ok 2 32 / lift exit'. ninja -n lift_selftest: 'no work to do', 0.02 s.

/tmp/meas/conc.py: tails with 0 other builds are 34-42 s (5 builds). cg-01 d789 and lg-01b 9191 had 2.0 other builds (1.6-1.7 in pdb_layout), effective cores 1.24-1.29. Pearson(tail, other pdbl+cc) = 0.81.
gate.log over all full dirs: 30x 'gate ok', 30x 'selftest ok', pdb_layout 0 errors (26x 1763/6522, 4x 1790/6567).
Layout dump sha256 is the same in d789726 and e76b748: CryptoKey e218e8bec3e6efd6, CacheD df9ca6ebf7c56032, LobbyDaemon.cpp 3deec1a939e670b5.
ledger/events.jsonl: 5 v2b cards landed (cg-02 3, merge-01 1, merge-02 2, pod-01 2, wmain-01 1 full_build). Their 9 phased tails sum to 574 s, mean 63.8 s.
proposal:
Make pdb_layout content-keyed. Extend buildcache.py with a `layout` kind, and make the clang_dump in tools/pdb_layout.py go through a shim. One option is a `PDB_LAYOUT_DUMP` launcher env, set in gate_fast.sh:57-61 next to CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER.

Per TU, the key is the cc key with the argv of the dump: the compiler file id, cwd, argv including '/Zs -Xclang -fdump-record-layouts-complete', and the preprocessed-source sha256. Direct mode can reuse the cc manifest. The value is the parsed lift_records list as JSON, not the 0.5-0.9 M-char raw dump. Optional: add a whole-run verdict key: sha256 of all per-TU keys + resym dump hashes + pdb_layout.py/pdbq.py hashes + own_names input. On a hit, print the stored output and rc.

Expected result:
- The warm tail goes from 80 s median / 178 s max to about 4 s ❓. That saves 76 s median and 174 s max per full build.
- It frees about 213 CPU-s per build for the other slots.
- It saves about 215-650 s per 6-card wave on the land chain. That is 6-18 % of the 1-hour goal.
- The verdict stays the same by construction, because the dumps are byte-identical for the same input (checked on 2 clones).

Before rollout, run gate_fast.sh once with the cache and once without on 2 builds, for example cg-01/d789 and merge-02/e76b. Compare rc and the 'selftest ok', 'pdb_layout: … 0 errors' and 'gate ok' lines.

The fallback is cheaper but saves less. Start tools/gate_extra.sh in the background after the ninja build, and wait for it after parity_sh. That saves at most 45 s median and 103 s max, and it keeps the CPU load.

grade.lesson: In a warm v2b gate_sh, tools/pdb_layout.py takes almost all of the tail after compile: it runs uncached clang-cl /Zs on all 345 TUs on os.cpu_count() threads, so it costs about 213 CPU-s and makes parallel slots compete for CPU.
grade.notes:
Checks I ran:
- gate_extra.sh:5-7 runs run_selftest.sh and then pdb_layout.py. pdb_layout.py:128-136 holds clang_dump with /Zs -fdump-record-layouts-complete. :190-191 uses ThreadPoolExecutor(os.cpu_count()). Only resym_dump has a cache (:55-60).
- cg-01/full-d789726212: gate_sh runs 003.66→221.64 (218 s). 391 cc events have t 005.14 to 043.85. The newest .exe/.lib is CacheGate.exe at 044. So about 177.6 s run after the last output. gate.log has 'selftest ok', 'pdb_layout: 1763 classes, 6522 members … 0 errors' and 'gate ok'.
- I ran one awk over all the phased builds. It gives 30 builds, not 28, ❓ maybe because of how the dirs are counted. Tail after the last output: min 34.8 s, median 80.4 s, max 177.6 s. This matches the solver.

Not checked:
- The 0.604 CPU-s per TU and the contention correlation r=0.81. I did not rerun them. They look plausible.

Weak points:
- The change was not run. The roughly 4 s residual and the 215-650 s wave saving are estimates.
- The second determinism check only covers 3 TUs.

The proposal fits the evidence. A cache keyed on the content of each TU removes about 76 s median and 174 s max per build. It also frees CPU for the other slots.

subject: cost
question: The 8 v2b author.py runs used 11 Claude sessions. In each session the prompt grows linearly from 15-36k tokens to 51-110k tokens. The size is cache_read + cache_creation + input of each new assistant message.id in /data/parity-v2/author/lift-lobbydaemon-v2b-*/session-*.jsonl. Example: lg-01 grows from 30,071 to 110,181 tokens in 26 messages and hits the 100k context split. Because every turn reads the full prefix again, cache_read builds up much faster than the session length. lg-01b session 1 has 1.755M cache_read against only 74k cache_creation. With author.py:71 weights (1.25 × cache write, 0.1 × cache read, 5 × output), cache read is about 38 % of the 455k units of lg-01b. Most tool calls only gather context. Each session makes 12-23 Grep calls, 6-19 Read calls and only 1-15 Edit calls. No session runs gate.sh itself, because author.py builds outside the session (build-gate-rNN.log). The first prompt also varies: pod-01 starts at 31-36k tokens (prompt-01.md is 7,152 words), and lg-01b starts at 18k tokens. Questions: (1) For each session, sort the tool_result blocks that cause the per-turn growth by tool and target (Grep over the whole tree, Read of a full .cpp or .h, Read of orig asm or funcdiff dumps, python3 helpers). Give the tokens each one adds to the prefix and the cache_read units it causes over the remaining turns (growth × turns left × 0.1). (2) How many of these Read and Grep results fetch data that author.py already has before the session starts? Examples are the card item list, orig and lift disassembly of each item, the lift source span of each symbol, and its callers. author.py could put this data into prompt-01.md once. (3) Measure the cut in units for each MATCH for two fixes. Fix A: pre-seed the symbol spans and diffs in the prompt, and cap Grep (files_with_matches or head_limit) and Read (limit) for the author tool path. Fix B: author.py starts a new session with a digest when the prompt passes about 60k tokens, and does not wait for the 100k split. Compare both with the 84k nocr per MATCH goal. (4) Did lg-01 park (no_change at turn 26) only because of this growth? Would Fix A have kept it under 100k? Give the wall seconds that this saves from the 1-hour wave goal.
why: The earlier lessons covered general-purpose subagent cache writes, duplicate reviews and parks. They did not cover the author.py path, which is the path v2 must use. In that path, the cost comes from turn-by-turn growth of the prompt, and Grep and Read results cause most of the growth. Cache read is paid on every later turn, so each early large result multiplies its cost. One concrete change in author.py (pre-seed spans, cap Grep and Read, digest handoff at about 60k tokens) can cut cache-read and cache-write units for each MATCH. The same change also removes context-split parks like lg-01 (417,607 units with no result), so it helps both the 84k-per-MATCH goal and the wall-time goal.
answer:
Scope: 11 author.py sessions (8 v2b cards), 268 turns, 983,794 nocr (cache write + output), 3,313,267 cost units. Ledger credit for v2b is 10 MATCH, so author nocr alone is 98.4k per MATCH. That is already above the 84k goal before you add reviews and builds.

KEY FACT 1. All 8 v2b runs used --no-packet. state.json opts.packet = False for all 8 cards. prompt-01.md still says "The packet at the end of this prompt holds … the compact pseudocode". The packet is not there. The sessions read the Hex-Rays cache themselves.

KEY FACT 2. nocr = input + cache_creation + output. Cache read is not in nocr. So for the 84k goal, a cut in cache read gives 0. Only a smaller final prompt per session (cache_creation ≈ last prompt; lg-01 cc 110,179 against last prompt 110,181) or less output helps.

(1) Growth by source (tokens added to the prompt; crU = growth × turns left × 0.1):
- In total, sessions grew 599,944 tokens. 266,785 of these (44 %) are prefetchable: hr pseudocode 129,427, Read of the card's own lift files 106,070, Grep or Bash for card symbol names 30,693. The rest is other Grep/Read/Bash (about 143k) and model output kept in context (about 190k).
- Cache read: 42 % comes from the first prompt and 58 % from growth.
- Read already uses a line limit in nearly every call (only 2 full reads in 11 sessions). A Read cap does not help.
- Grep content mode with no head_limit, over 1k tokens, adds 40,822 tokens of excess (pod-01 s1 alone: 19,620).
- Biggest sinks per session (grow tok / crU): lg-01 Read src.cpp 20,429/28,839 and Read hr 16,003/20,299. lg-01a Read hr 22,555/38,608 and Read src.cpp 18,731/36,057. lg-01c Read src.cpp 21,337/40,592. pod-01 s1 Grep tree content 25,094/21,822. scd-01a Read hr 15,853/27,504.

(2) 92 of 268 turns (34 %) hold only prefetchable calls (hr, card lift file, card symbol grep). That is lg-01 14/26, scd-01b 11/18, scd-01a 14/33, pod-01 s1 12/27. author_packet.py already gives pseudocode, PDB class, lift files (a long file is a stub list only) and callees. It gives no per-symbol line span. The run turned it off.

(3) Model on the real per-message prompt series. Fix A: seed min(P, 14k) per session, remove prefetchable growth and its turns, and cap content Grep at about 1k tokens. Fix B: split at 60k with the measured 5,359-token handoff of pod-01 x01.
| | nocr/MATCH | cu/MATCH |
| --- | --- | --- |
| measured | 98.4k | 331k |
| Fix A | 73.2k (−25.6 %) | 219k (−34 %) |
| Fix B | 118.6k (+20.6 %) | 324k (−2 %) |
Fix A meets the 84k goal for author tokens, with 10.8k left for reviews (L4: under 1 %) and repairs. Fix B fails it: each extra session writes the first prompt and the handoff to cache again (+20-42k nocr each), and the cache-read saving does not count in nocr.

(4) lg-01 parked because of growth, but not only because of growth. It made 0 Edit calls in 26 turns, on a card with 17 functions (prompt 6,966 words). The split fired at 110,181 tokens with no change, so it parked as no_change. Under Fix A the modeled last prompt is 76,507 tokens. That is under 100k, with about 7 turns of room at the measured growth of about 3.1k tokens per turn. ❓ The model does not show that 17 functions fit in those turns. The lg-01 chain (lg-01 + lg-01a/b/c) cost 1,697,519 cu. The pre-proof gain of lg-01b and lg-01c was 0.

Wall time: Fix A gives 0 s on builds plus tests. It removes about 8.5 s per removed turn (lg-01: 222.25 s for 26 turns). On the critical path of the 3 parallel author batches this is about 300 s (pod-01 19 turns, lg-01a 10 turns, lg-01b 10 turns), or about 8 % of the 1-hour goal. Each park that you avoid removes one re-card gap: lg-01 parked at 13:53:53 and lg-01a started at 14:21:16, which is 1,643 s ❓ (operator time, not engine time).
evidence: state.json opts.packet=False for all 8 v2b cards (python read of author/lift-lobbydaemon-v2b-*/state.json); author.py:1582 o['packet'] = not no_packet
prompt-01.md line 32 promises a packet; grep finds no packet section in lg-01 or lg-01b prompt-01.md
ledger events.jsonl kind=author v2b: 11 sessions, cc+out = 983,794, cost_units sum ≈ 3.31M; lg-01 417,607 cu, status split
ledger credit v2b: pod-01 4, wmain-01 3, cg-02 1, merge-01 0, merge-02 2 = 10 MATCH
REPORT.md:1 nocr = input + output + cache creation (cache read is not in nocr)

Growth attribution (message.id prompt deltas minus message_delta output): 599,944 growth, 266,785 prefetchable (hr 129,427 / card lift files 106,070 / symbol greps 30,693), Grep content excess 40,822, 92 of 268 turns all-prefetch
Cache read share: 42 % from the first prompt × turns, 58 % from growth
lg-01 state park: 'context split with no change (round 1): prompt 110181 tokens > 100000 (turn 26)'; 0 Edit/Write calls in session
ledger lg-01 author.session 222.25 s, commit done 13:53:53; lg-01a session file starts 14:21:16
pod-01 x01: first prompt 36,486 against 31,127 (handoff 5,359 tokens); lg-01a/b/c/scd ran with ctx_split 160000
author_packet.py:47 SHARD_TOKENS=14000; docstring: long lift files only as stub list (no symbol span)
proposal:
Change: turn the packet back on and add symbol spans. Do not use the 60k split.
1. Operator route (docs/AUTHOR-ROUTE.md and the v2b batch command): do not pass --no-packet. Make author.py refuse --no-packet for a card with more than 3 scope rows. A prompt must not claim a packet that is not there.
2. author_packet.py build_one: for each card ID, add a 'span' part: the file:line range of the lift body (from the RVA scan that already exists) plus up to 80 lines of its text, and its callers (Grep -n of the short name in src, max 10 lines). Keep the 14k shard cap so a card with too many functions makes more shards (this splits lg-01 into 2 shards before round 1).
3. author.py PreToolUse rule for the author tool path: give Grep output_mode=content a default head_limit=40 and refuse a Grep with no path under src/ (whole-tree content grep).
4. Keep ctx_split at 100k. Do not add a 60k digest handoff: it adds +20.6 % nocr.
Expected gain (modeled on the 11 real sessions): nocr per MATCH 98.4k → 73.2k (−25 %, under the 84k goal), cost units 331k → 219k per MATCH (−34 %), 92 fewer turns (−34 %), about 300 s less author critical path (about 8 % of the 1-hour goal; 0 s on builds plus tests), and lg-01's last prompt goes from 110k to about 77k, under the split.

grade.lesson: Divide author tokens only by the MATCH credit of the same cards: of the 8 v2b author.py cards only pod-01 landed (ref_match 4), so author nocr per MATCH is about 246k, not 98.4k.
grade.notes: Verified: opts.packet False for all 8 cards (default True, author.py:154); prompt-01.md:32 claims a packet that is not there; 11 sessions with 268 unique msg ids; the first/last prompts match (lg-01 30,071 -> 110,181, 0 edits); ledger cost units 3,313,839 and nocr 984,338 (claim 983,794); CTX_SPLIT 100k at author.py:152; weights at author.py:80 (the answer cites lines 71 and 1156-1157 wrongly); SHARD_TOKENS 14000. Main flaw: the 10-MATCH denominator comes from pod-01 4 + wmain-01 3 + cg-02 1 + merge-02 2. wmain/cg-02/merge have no author.py session, and merge-03c (5) is left out. Of the author.py cards only pod-01 landed. Real author nocr/MATCH is about 246k, so Fix A gives about 183k and fails the 84k goal; the 'meets goal' conclusion is false. lg-01a/scd-01a parked on main-moved and pod-01 on review accept, not on growth. The per-result attribution (266,785 prefetchable tokens, 92 turns) was not re-checked. The proposal (packet on, refuse --no-packet, Grep head_limit) is still useful and cheap.

subject: fleet
question:
The v2b wave ran 28 full_build steps, and all 28 ran on the local host. The fleet's remote slots stayed almost idle. Why did the router keep them local, and which routing change gives the shortest wave?

Facts:

| Fact | Source |
| --- | --- |
| 28 full_build events between 14:01 and 15:26Z. They took 7,860 s in total (61–1,358 s each). The first two started together and took 1,017 s (pod-01) and 1,358 s (cg-01). | /data/parity-v2/ledger/events.jsonl, step=full_build |
| In the same window, remote.jsonl has only 2 rows. Both are author gates on build3 (lg-01b 194.6 s, lg-01c 140.8 s). No full_build row exists. | /data/parity-v2/cardrun/slotq/remote.jsonl (7 rows in total) |
| `remote_job` returns None when remote is off, when prio == 'land', or when the command matches neither `build_job` nor `linked_job`. | parityctl/slotq.py:925-937 |
| `build_direct` serves cardrun full_build and base_build. The caller "holds a local slot already". The command tries one free remote slot, and the local slot stays held while the remote build runs. | slotq.py:1148-1178 |
| build2 has 4 remote slots and build3 has 6. | /data/parity-v2/hosts.json |

Questions:
(a) For each of the 28 full_build steps, find which exit of `remote_job` stopped remote dispatch. The options are: remote off in the cardrun env, prio land, no `build_job`/`linked_job` match, a `remote_ready` refusal (find the "slotrun: no remote build:" line in the card logs), or no free host. Count the steps for each cause.
(b) Why did pod-01 and cg-01 take 1,017 s and 1,358 s, when the other 26 steps had a median of about 220 s? Was the cause a cold vsobj or build cache, or two runs at the same time on 8 cores, or something else? Give the evidence from the card logs or gate.phases.
(c) Use the measured remote gate times (136–195 s on build3) and the pull time. Simulate the wave for three cases: (1) card-prio full_build may go remote, (2) also release the local slot while the job runs remote, (3) add the dedicated server as a fourth host. Give the wave seconds saved for each case. Say how much of the 3,600 s goal each case wins. Each case adds 0 tokens per MATCH, so confirm that no model call changes.
(d) Land jobs "never go remote" (slotq.py:926). Give the reason for this rule (trust, receipt or reproducibility). What check, for example a matching obj/PDB hash for each target, would make a remote land build safe?
why: L5 of measure says that full_build is the main step on the v2b land chain. The data shows 7,860 s of full_build, all on one 8-core host, while 10 remote slots were idle. Earlier lessons covered objsync, cool-down, slot sizing and vsobj cold start for remote gates. They did not ask why the biggest build step never reaches the fleet. There are three possible causes: an eligibility gate in remote_job, a local slot that stays held during a remote run in build_direct, and the land-never-remote rule. Each cause has its own fix. The fixes cost 0 tokens, and they can save a large part of the about 2,967 s gap between the 6,567 s v2b wave and the 3,600 s goal.
answer:
(a) None of the 5 remote_job exits applies. All 28 v2b full_build steps (28/28) never reached remote_job. cardrun runs COMMANDS['full_build'] = bare `bash gate_fast.sh CLONE HOME` (cardrun.py:150) through run_cmd/run_limited (cardrun.py:669-678). cardrun.py has no slotq call, and `git log -S slotq` on cardrun.py is empty. build_direct (slotq.py:1148, commit 47a95e0d, 00:51Z) has no caller. All 31 v2b full_build logs are 100 bytes (only the disk_guard line) and have 0 'slotrun:' lines. If the step were routed, all 28 would pass: the build_job form matches (slotq.py:608), BUILD_HOSTNAME is present (gate_fast.sh:51), the clone has no alternates (cardrun.py:753), the home folder exists, and prio defaults to 'card' (slotq.py:121).
(b) The 1,017 s and 1,358 s are mostly NOT build time. In-sandbox time (phase start to gate.rc mtime) was 433 s for cg-01 and 397 s for pod-01. Of that, cold vsobj (restore+record) took 262 s and 231 s; later builds took 1-44 s. The two sandbox builds overlapped for only about 93 s. Then each step waited after gate.rc: 922 s for cg-01 and 618 s for pod-01. Both ended in the same second (gate.log and ledger at 1795702684 = 14:18:04Z). The other 26 builds have a tail of 1-4 s. After gate.rc, gate_fast.sh runs only gc, cp and echo (gate_fast.sh:72-76). gc removed 0 entries and takes no lock (buildcache.py:892-914). The cause of the shared stall is unknown ❓ (pause, SIGSTOP or I/O stall).
(c) Estimates from per-step chains, not a full simulation. Remote time is 141-195 s from start to end including the pull (remote.jsonl), plus about 100 s for a cold namespace. At most 4 full_builds ran at the same time.
- Case 1 (card full_build goes remote): about 500 s if the 14:18 stall still applies, about 1,400 s if remote builds avoid it ❓. That is 17-47 % of the 2,967 s gap and 14-39 % of the 3,600 s goal. Builds shorter than 141 s (5 of 28) should stay local.
- Case 2 (release the local slot): about 0-200 s ❓. The held slot is a cardrun card slot, and the ledger shows no card waiting for one.
- Case 3 (fourth host): about 0 s at v2b load, because 10 remote slots exceed the peak of 4 builds plus 2 author gates. It only adds survival when a host dies; build2 alone still covers the peak of 4.
All three cases add 0 tokens per MATCH: review is a separate step and BUILD_HOSTNAME keeps the bytes the same. Do not edit COMMANDS['full_build']: tool_digest (cardrun.py:809) includes it, so base strict data would be rebuilt. That costs time but no model tokens.
(d) The code gives no reason. slotq.py:47 and :926 only state the rule ❓. The likely reason is the receipt: the land build produces the accept result that goes to main. The remote path checks the rev and the tool and input digests (remote_build.py:52, :1102-1104) but does not check the output bytes. A safe remote land needs a per-exe sha256 of the 5 exes and the funcdiff JSON that equals a second independent result: a cached build of the same tree hash, or a local link-only rebuild. A two-host canary on one rev must first show identical bytes.
evidence: cardrun.py:150 COMMANDS['full_build'] = ['bash','{parityctl}/gate_fast.sh','{clone}','{home}']; cardrun.py:669-678 runs it via run_limited, no slotq
grep slotq parityctl/cardrun.py: no match; git log -S slotq -- parityctl/cardrun.py: empty; build_direct callers: only slotq.py:1407 CLI
31 v2b full_build-*.log files, each 100 bytes (disk_guard admit line), 0 contain 'slotrun'
remote.jsonl 7 rows; only 2 in the wave (build3 gate lg-01b 194.6 s, lg-01c 140.8 s)
ledger: 28 full_build, sum 7,860 s, median of the other 26 = 208 s, max 4 concurrent, time with >=1 build running 4,456 s of a 5,437 s span
cg-01 gate.phases: in-sandbox 433 s (vsobj_restore 195 + record 67); gate.rc mtime 1795701762, gate.log 1795702684 -> 922 s tail
pod-01 ef90562020: in-sandbox 397 s (vsobj 172+59); gate.rc 1795702066 -> 618 s tail; all other 26 builds have a 1-4 s tail
gate_fast.sh:72-76: after gate.rc only buildcache gc, cp, echo; gc removed 0 entries ({'entries':9154,'removed':0}); buildcache.py:892-914 gc has no lock
cardrun.py:809 tool_digest includes cfg['commands']['full_build']
slotq.py:47 and 926: land never remote, no reason given; remote_build.py:52,1102-1104 checks tool/input digests only
proposal: In cardrun.run_cmd (cardrun.py:669), for name=='full_build' and a step that does not start with land_, put [python3,-I,slotq.py,build] in front of argv at run time with SLOTRUN_PRIO=card. Do not edit COMMANDS, so tool_digest and the checker digest stay the same. Send a build remote only when 2 or more local full_builds already run, so builds shorter than 141 s stay local. Write the remote host into the ledger build event. Expected gain: about 500-1,400 s of the 6,567 s wave (17-47 % of the gap), 0 tokens per MATCH. Find the cause of the 14:18:04 stall (time buildcache gc on its own) before you rely on the upper estimate. Leave land builds local until a per-exe sha256 check across two hosts exists.

grade.lesson: Check that a router has a caller before you find which exit refused a job, because cardrun runs full_build as bare gate_fast.sh and never calls slotq.
grade.notes:
Verified claims:
- cardrun.py:149 sets COMMANDS['full_build'] = bash gate_fast.sh {clone} {home}. cardrun.py:669-678 runs it through run_limited.
- A grep for slotq in cardrun.py finds nothing.
- build_direct is called only from the slotq.py:1407 CLI and a test (tests/test_slotq_remote.py:581).
- remote_job is at slotq.py:925-937, and it matches the description.
- tool_digest is at cardrun.py:808-812 and includes commands['full_build']. The advice not to edit COMMANDS is correct.
- There are 31 v2b full_build-*.log files, all exactly 100 bytes (the disk_guard admit line). 0 of them contain 'slotrun'.
- The ledger has 30 v2b full_build events, sum 8,600 s. The two over 900 s ended at 1795702684-85. The answer says 28 events and 7,860 s, so it must use a window filter. I did not check that filter ❓.
- remote.jsonl has 7 rows.
- For cg-01: gate.rc mtime is 1795701762 and gate.log mtime is 1795702684, a 922 s tail. A later cg-01 build has a 2 s tail. After gate.rc, gate_fast.sh:73-76 runs only buildcache gc, cp and echo. The tail claim is confirmed.

Weak points:
- The answer leaves the shared 14:18:04 stall without a cause. buildcache gc over about 9.1k entries is the obvious suspect, and the answer could have timed it cheaply.
- Part (c) gives estimates, not a simulation, and the range is wide (500-1,400 s).
- Part (d) gives no reason from the code. Its receipt argument is a reasonable guess.
- The proposal is sound: wrap at run time, keep the digest the same, add 0 tokens. Its gain is uncertain until the stall is explained.

subject: safety
question:
Remote builds are the main speed lever for the 1 h goal. A cold build3 gate run takes 135.8 s and 149.1 s (cardrun remote.json, 2026-11-26T14:43-14:44Z). A loaded local gate takes 196-229 s. A dedicated server is coming soon. Does this shortcut keep the "no false MATCH, reproducible proof" guarantee when a host changes after its setup?

Facts that I found:
- slotq.py:39-48 sends each `gate_fast.sh` job to a free remote host automatically. Linked and preview builds can also go remote (slotq.py:50-59). Only land jobs stay local.
- remote_build.py:1109-1110 lists the MUST items: wine, bwrap, toolchain, uv_site, resymc, wine_tar, llvm_pdbutil, python3 and others. It also adds the `input:` digests of the original exe/pdb files (remote_build.py:1113-1115). The code compares them only in the manual `remote_build.py check --host H` command (remote_build.py:1256-1260). The setup runs it once, as its last step (remote_host_setup.sh:21, 91). I found no call of `check` or `probe` on the per-job path in slotq.py or remote_build.py `run`.
- `<clone>/../remote.json` records the host, rev, rc and seconds, but no environment digest. proof.py R8 (input_bind, proof.py:28-32) binds gate.rev and the sha256 of the signal files only. proof.py has no host, toolchain or Wine id.
- The object cache key does hold the host name, the Wine runtime and the prefix (buildcache.build_env_id, buildcache.py:164-172; vs_namespace, buildcache.py:477). But objcache.py:16 keys the toolchain by path, size and mtime only, and `rsync -a` keeps mtime. Also, the funcdiff/capstone libs (uv_site) and the original exe/pdb copies on the remote host are not in any per-job key.
- docs/REMOTE-HOST.md §7 proves that remote and local builds are equal only for the self-test revs, at setup time.

Question:
(a) Make a table of the MUST and input items. For each item, say whether a silent change on one host after setup (apt upgrade of wine or llvm, a new uv_site, a replaced original pdb, a toolchain file edited with the same size and mtime) can change the exe/pdb bytes, the PDB symbol names (for example ?A0x anonymous-namespace names), or the funcdiff verdict. Also say whether a per-job key would turn that change into a miss, or whether it could give a remote MATCH that a local build of the same rev does not give.
(b) Measure the seconds of one `probe(SshTransport(build3))` call. Then compare two fixes, and give the seconds per job and per wave for each:
   1. Run `check` before each remote job, or once per wave per host.
   2. Write a host env digest (the hash of the MUST rows) into remote.json. Bind that digest in proof R8, so that integrate.py refuses a proof that has no digest or has a digest that differs from the local host.
   Use the number of remote jobs in the v2b wave for the per-wave cost.
(c) Propose a reproducibility audit. For example: rebuild K landed proofs per wave on a second host (or locally), and compare them with the §7 rules. Give K, its build seconds, and the chance that it catches one drifted host in a wave.
(d) Name a test that proves the fix. For example: use `--transport local` with a fake host root. Swap one uv_site file or one original .pdb. Then show that the job refuses, or that proof R8 fails, and that no MATCH credit lands.
Say how much of the 1 h goal the remote lane wins (about 50-90 s per job compared with a loaded local gate). Say how many of those seconds the safe version gives back.
why: Earlier rounds covered the fd cache key, the base cache key and the review carry. None of them checked the remote build lane. That lane is now on by default and gives the biggest build-time cut toward 1 h, and a dedicated server will add more remote slots. Today host equality is proven only once, at setup, and a proof does not record which host or environment built its signals. So host drift (in the toolchain, Wine, funcdiff libs or the original files) can give a MATCH that does not reproduce on another host, and R8 cannot detect it. That breaks the "reproducible proof" and "no false MATCH" guarantees. A cheap env digest in remote.json, bound in proof R8, plus a small audit keeps the speed and closes the gap.
answer: No. The remote lane breaks the 'reproducible proof' guarantee when a host changes after its setup. Host equality is checked only by the manual `check` command (remote_build.py:1256-1260). The receipt records no environment (remote_build.py:474-476), and R8 binds only gate.rev (proof.py:248-273). A cache key change only makes a cache miss. The job then recomputes on the changed host, so a changed Wine, Wine prefix, toolchain, llvm-pdbutil, uv_site or original pdb can give a remote MATCH that a local build of the same rev does not give. The toolchain is the worst row: the probe hashes path and size only (remote_build.py:1102), and objcache hashes path, size and mtime, so an edit that keeps size and mtime passes both. In v2b the risk was not used yet: only 2 jobs ran remote (author gates on build3, 194.6 s and 140.8 s in slotq/remote.jsonl), and all 30 card gates ran locally (median 237 s). Card full builds can go remote (cardrun.py:150 matches slotq.py:39-48). Measured costs: probe on build3 1.66 s cold and 0.48 s warm, local probe 0.6 s, toolchain content hash 17.65 s, ctime scan 0.04 s. Fix 1 (check per job) adds 1.1-2.3 s per job and binds nothing. Fix 1b (once per wave per host) costs 2.4 s per wave but misses drift during the wave. Fix 2 (env digest in the job, bound in R8, compared by integrate) adds about 0.6 s per job, about 1.2 s for the v2b wave and about 0 s on the land chain, and it closes the gap. The audit rebuilds K=1 landed proof per remote host plus 1 local proof on another host and compares exe, pdb and funcdiff.json. It costs about 420 slot-seconds off the chain and catches a host that drifts on every build with a chance of about 1.0. The remote lane saves about 96 s per job (237 s local against about 141 s remote), which is about 740 s per wave ❓ or about 25 % of the 2,967 s cut needed. The safe version gives back less than 1 % of that saving.

proposal: Make each build record its environment and make the proof check it. (1) gate_fast.sh writes gate.env with the MUST rows of the probe and the input sha256 rows. The toolchain row becomes path+size+mtime, plus a content-hash memo (17.65 s) that runs again only when the ctime scan (0.04 s) changes. Leave out host, because BUILD_HOSTNAME is already the dispatcher name. Local and remote builds both write the file. (2) remote_build.run_job adds gate.env to GATE_FILES and copies its digest into remote.json 'env'. (3) proof.py R8 bind_build reads gate.env and fails input_bind when the file is missing or not equal for all 5 exes; it records build.env. (4) integrate.check_proof refuses a proof whose build.env differs from the local digest (memoised, 0.6 s). (5) After each wave, rebuild K = 1 landed proof per remote host plus 1 local proof on another host, off the chain (about 420 slot-seconds). Compare them with remote_build.compare and a byte compare of EXE.funcdiff.json. Test: in tests/test_remote_build.py, use --transport local with a fake HOME that has a changed capstone file, and a PARITY_PROJ copy of ida/lift with one changed byte in a pdb. Expect a different gate.env, an R8 input_bind 'env' reason, integrate Refused and no ledger credit; with no swap the proof passes. Gain: the remote lane keeps about 96 s per job (about 740 s per wave ❓, about 25 % of the gap to 1 h), costs about 0.6 s per job and 0 model tokens, and turns every drift in the table into a refused proof, not a false MATCH.

grade.lesson: The remote receipt and proof R8 bind only gate.rev, and the toolchain probe hashes only path and size, so a build host that changes after setup can give a remote MATCH that no local build of the same rev reproduces.
grade.notes:
I checked the main claims myself.
- remote_build.py:1102: the toolchain probe row is `find -printf "%P %s"`. It hashes path and size only, not content or mtime.
- :1109-1110: MUST list confirmed.
- :474-476: the receipt holds host, slot, rev, rc, seconds, obj and finished. It holds no environment.
- grep: `check(` and `probe(` occur only at :1123, :1133 and :1260 (manual CLI). slotq has only lock probes. There is no per-job check.
- proof.py:248-273 bind_build binds gate.rev only.
- integrate.py has no env check; :189 checks checker_digest only.
- objcache.py:16 keys the toolchain by path, size and mtime.
- slotq/remote.jsonl: the v2b wave has 2 remote gate jobs on build3 (194.6 s, 140.8 s). find gives 2 remote.json files. Card full-* folders have 0 remote.json.

Weak points:
- I did not rerun the probe timings (1.66/0.48 s) or the 17.65 s toolchain hash. The ssh probe needs owner consent.
- The 96 s per job saving uses the faster remote run (141 s). The mean of the 2 remote runs is about 168 s, so the saving is closer to about 70 s per job.
- The 740 s per wave is a projection; the solver marked it ❓. In v2b, only about 2×(70-96) s was won, because the card gates ran locally.
- "Catch chance ≈1.0" assumes a host that drifts on every build. A drift that affects only some functions is caught less often.

Fix 2 (env digest bound in R8 and compared in integrate) is sound and cheap. Main verdict: no, the guarantee does not hold today. The solver is correct.

subject: measure
question:
The ledger cannot time the review step, and it cannot split review tokens into "led to a MATCH" and "wasted". Evidence:
(a) /data/parity-v2/ledger/events.jsonl has 28 live v2b `review` events. Review events have no `seconds` field. ledger.record_build (ledger.py:401) is the only writer that stores seconds. All review events of one card share one `at`. For example, the 7 merge-03b events all have at=1795706889, and the 4 merge-03 events all have at=1795706884. So `at` is the time of the export, not the time of each item.
(b) The per-card sqlite stores the real times. cardrun/slot2/lift-lobbydaemon-v2b-merge-03b/ledger.sqlite tables `review` and `review_attempt` have one `at` per item: 847.09, 850.08, 861.19, 874.87, 879.59, 889.06 (offsets from 1795706000). The review logs start at 825.39 and 826.97 (logs/review-*.log names). So 5 model reviews ran one after the other, about 10-14 s each, for about 64 s in total. The ledger loses this.
(c) Precheck rejects are written as review events with model=None, raw={'unknown':0}, unpriced=['unknown'] and 0 tokens (merge-03b P2_cc, merge-03d). Carried reviews (merge-03c and merge-03d: 10 events) have tokens 0 and raw=null. So the review count (28) mixes model draws, deterministic prechecks and carries.
(d) merge-03b has 6 accepts (about 3k tokens each), but its sqlite `credit` table is empty and state.json says result=blocked. So those review tokens bought no MATCH, and no ledger event says this.
Questions:
(1) For the 2026-11-26 v2b wave, use the per-card ledger.sqlite files (review, review_attempt, credit) under cardrun/slot*/ and the review-*.log start times. Give: review wall seconds per card and per item, the share of that time on the land critical path, and the review nocr tokens split into (i) items on cards that got credit, (ii) items on blocked or parked cards, (iii) carried items (0 tokens). How many review tokens per credited MATCH does this give, and how does it compare with author nocr per MATCH?
(2) The reviews run serially. If they ran in parallel (one call per item), how many seconds would each card save, and how many seconds of the 1 h goal is that over the wave?
(3) What is the smallest export change? For example: the ledger review event copies the per-item `at` and adds `t0` (from review_attempt or the log start) and `seconds`; it adds `draw` = model | precheck | carry so that prechecks and carries are not counted as model reviews; and the card writes a credit event with match_gain=0 when the result is blocked. With that change, can one query give review seconds per card and wasted review tokens per wave?
why: Earlier rounds measured builds (L3), author tokens (L4) and wave wall time (L5), but review was never measured. Review is a model step on the land chain. Its time and tokens are in the per-card sqlite but are lost or flattened in the shared ledger. So no one can prove whether parallel review, or skipping review on blocked cards, saves seconds or tokens. The 6 accepts on the blocked merge-03b card are a concrete case of review tokens with no MATCH.
answer:
Measured from the per-card sqlite files, the review-*.log files and the item-*.json files of the v2b wave (845 to 7519 s = 6,674 s).
(1) Review wall time is about 218 s in total (3.3 % of the wave). Landed cards use about 73 s of it (1.1 %). With the 66 s review of merge-03b, whose receipts merge-03c carried to land, it is about 139 s. A model draw takes 3.8 to 10.4 s (mean 7.66 s, 16 draws, 122.5 s). A carry takes about 1.1 s per item. A precheck reject takes 0 s of model time and about 3 s for the bundle. Review nocr is 38,086 tokens. By card outcome: (i) credited cards 15,893; (ii) blocked cards 22,193; (iii) 10 carries and 2 prechecks at 0 tokens. The outcome split is misleading. merge-03b has 5 accepts, not 6, and its 11,155 tokens bought 5 MATCH through the carry into merge-03c. By value: 17,207 nocr led to 8 review-accept MATCH (2,151 per MATCH), 13,679 nocr went to rejects, and 7,200 nocr went to merge-03, which reviewed the same 4 keys as merge-03b at the same time (all 7 key parts equal). Review costs 2.5k nocr per credited MATCH (38,086/15). Author costs 65.6k (984,338/15). Author plus review is 68.2k, below the manual 84k ❓ (other token sources not counted).
(2) Parallel review saves about 40 to 50 s on merge-03b and about 40 s on merge-03. Those two cards ran at the same time and both were blocked. The wave saves at most 45 s (at most 1.25 % of 1 h). The land chain saves 0 s, because every landed card had at most 1 model draw per run.
(3) Yes, one query works after 3 small changes: a review step event, per-item at/t0/seconds/draw in export_reviews, and a blocked credit event. The 'credited' test must follow the carried_from refs, or the merge-03b tokens count as waste by mistake.
evidence: cardrun.py:640: only gate, full_build, base_build, strict and proof get a ledger build event. The review step has no seconds in the ledger.

ledger.py:627-660 export_reviews writes all events of a card in one append_many call, so they share one 'at'. ledger.py:249 keeps a valid caller 'at'. Line 650 skips local carries, so they get no event.
merge-03b ledger.sqlite review table: 5 model accepts and 1 precheck reject (LobbyGate HandleLobbyGate_HelloReq). The credit table is empty.
Ledger seq 666-670 (merge-03c) and seq 671-675 (merge-03d) have carried_from = refs of seq 650-655 (merge-03b). merge-03c credit: ref_match 5, review_accept 5, landed at 1795707519.
Ledger keys of seq 646-649 (merge-03) and 650/652/653/655 (merge-03b) have no differing parts. Both review logs start at 6825.17 and 6825.39 (offsets from 1795700000).

state.json review step seconds: merge-03b 65.95, merge-03 60.78, wmain-01 19.42, pod-02 9.38, cg-02 9.33, merge-03d 7.54, pod-01 6.62, merge-03c 5.74. Log-only earlier runs: pod-01 10.5, cg-02 14.0, merge-02 7.6.

The receipt 'at' of merge-03 and merge-03b agree within 3 ms (6847.087/6847.090 and 6874.874/6874.874), 10.3 s and 6.4 s after the item-file writes. The databases are separate, so this is a shared stall ❓.

Meter rule (meter.py:16, 155-167): nocr = input - cached + cache_creation + output. Review nocr is 38,086 tokens. Author nocr is 984,338 tokens over 11 events (L4 rule for split sessions). Credit events give 15 MATCH (4+3+1+0+2+5).
receipts.reviews (receipts.py:253) does not return 'at'. review_digest (review.py:218) hashes the behaviour constants, not the file bytes.
proposal: Change 1: in cardrun.py:640, add 'review' to the step tuple, so every review run writes ledger kind=build step=review with seconds, including reruns that state.json drops. In ledger.summarize (ledger.py:742), add step 'review' to review_seconds, not to build_seconds. Change 2: in ledger.export_reviews (ledger.py:627), read the receipt 'at' of each item. Set event at = that receipt at, t0 = the receipt at of the item before it (or the step start, which cardrun s_review gives as a new argument), seconds = at - t0, and draw = 'model' when model and reply_digest are set, else 'precheck'. In carry_into (ledger.py:620), set draw='carry'. Also write an event with draw='carry' for local carries, which line 650 skips today. Do not edit review.py. Change 3: let record_credit (ledger.py:406) accept state='blocked' with ref_match=0, and call it from cardrun.finish (cardrun.py:1456) on a blocked result. Add one function, ledger.review_value(events). It checks each draw=model origin event: credited when its card landed with review_accept>0 or a carried copy points to its ref on a landed card; duplicate when another origin has the same key_id and overlaps it in time; otherwise reject or blocked waste. Size: about 40 lines ❓. Expected gain: no seconds by itself. It proves that review costs at most about 139 s of the land chain (about 2 % of the wave) and that parallel review wins at most 45 s (at most 1.25 % of the 1 h goal), so work on full_build instead. Next step: an in-flight key claim in global_carry (cardrun.py:1196). It would save the 7,200 nocr of concurrent duplicates (19 % of review nocr, less than 1 % of wave nocr) and 61 s of slot time per such pair.

grade.lesson: Follow the carried_from refs before you call review tokens wasted, because the merge-03b accepts bought 5 MATCH through the carry into merge-03c.
grade.notes:
I checked the main claim. It is correct.
- I read the per-card sqlite files with Python in read-only mode, because sqlite3 is not installed.
- Review nocr per card: pod-02 3838, cg-02 4704, merge-03b 11155, pod-01 4060, wmain-01 2497, merge-02 4632, merge-03 7200. Carries are 0. The sum is 38,086. The landed cards give 15,893 and the blocked cards give 22,193. These numbers agree with the answer.
- merge-03b has 5 model accepts and 1 precheck reject (model=None), and its credit table is empty. The answer is correct to change the question's "6 accepts" to 5.
- The ledger has 28 live review events, and 0 of them have a 'seconds' field. All events of one card share one 'at' (merge-03b 6, merge-03c 5, merge-03d 5+1, merge-03 4). The question's "7 merge-03b events" is wrong; the solver did not say this.
- The credit events give 4+3+1+0+2+5 = 15 MATCH. review_accept is 8 in total (merge-03c 5). Seq 666 and 671 have carried_from set, as the answer says.
- cardrun.py:640 has the step tuple without 'review'. export_reviews is at ledger.py:627, and the carry skip is at about line 650. Both are correct.
- state.json review seconds: merge-03b 65.95, merge-03 60.78, merge-03c 5.74. These are correct.
- Small error: the merge-03 review logs start at 6825.17 and 6826.52. The answer gives 6825.39, which is the merge-03b start.
- I did not check the 16 item-*.json draw seconds. I did not check the author nocr of 984,338.
Value: the proposal is a measurement change with about 40 lines ❓. It shows that review is at most about 2 % of the wave, and that parallel review wins at most 45 s. This is a useful negative result, because it sends the work to full_build. The proposal itself saves almost nothing against the 1 h goal.

subject: fleet
question:
The same card rev gets built more than once, in two lanes that do not share results. Can one result store that every host shares remove the duplicate builds, and how many wave seconds does that save?

Facts:

| Card pod-01, rev ef905620: author 148 + 145 s, then cardrun 1,017 + 213 s. | same |
| The buildonce store has 40 events: 29 built, 10 fail, and only 1 hit (ref). The store holds 265M on disk. | /data/parity-v2/build-results/events.jsonl, `du -sh` |

| cardrun full_build runs bare `bash gate_fast.sh {clone} {home}` and does not call buildonce. | parityctl/cardrun.py:150 |

| The store is local only (/data/parity-v2/build-results). The remote hosts do not read it. | buildonce.py docstring "Store:" |

(a) For each (card, rev) and each base main in the 2026-11-26 v2b wave, count how many times a gate_fast, ref or noref build ran on the same git tree. Use the ledger and the buildonce keys (`buildonce key gate CLONE` does not build). Give the sum of the duplicate build seconds.
(b) Why is the buildonce hit rate only 1 in 40? Sort the misses by cause: a different mode (ref/noref compared with gate), a key field that changes when the tree stays the same (for example scripts, env OVERLAY or a toolchain id), a cardrun path that bypasses buildonce, or a failed build. Give the key fields of two misses on the same tree, side by side.
(c) Propose one change. For example: cardrun full_build and base_build call `buildonce gate`, and the store gets a remote read/write path (rsync or a pull on a hit) so that build2, build3 and the dedicated server share it. Say which outputs the store must keep so that strict, proof and funcdiff can run without a rebuild (PDB, funcdiff signals, gate.phases). Check that the safety L6 rule still holds: a remote result must bind the toolchain hash, not only gate.rev.
(d) Simulate the wave with the change. Give the build seconds saved per card and per wave, and the part of the 3,600 s goal that it wins. Give the disk cost per entry (in MB) and the extra tokens per MATCH (expected 0, because no model call changes).
why: The ledger shows each card rev is built by author (buildonce ref/noref, about 300 s) and then built again by cardrun (bare gate_fast.sh, 1,017-1,358 s), and the base is rebuilt per card. buildonce exists to stop this, but its store has 1 hit in 40 events. cardrun.py:150 bypasses it, and the store is local only, so the remote hosts and the dedicated server cannot use it. Earlier questions covered the vsobj object cache, slots and routing. This one covers whole-result reuse across lanes and hosts. That can remove complete builds, not only make them faster.
answer: Yes, if the store key ignores Docs/ and README.md. In the 2026-11-26 v2b wave, cardrun built every one of the 7 base mains again, although each base main is the last landed card rev plus a docs-only commit (or, for 6824f3d0, a tree already in the store as gate entry 991996814e). The ref/noref-then-full_build cases (cg-01 1,358 s, pod-01 1,017 s) are a mode mismatch that a shared store does not fix.
